title: Tiered traffic-shedding and graceful fallback for overloaded inference paths
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Under transient overloads (region-wide capacity spikes or misbehaving clients), our serving layer experiences severe queue growth causing p95/p99 latency SLO violations and cascading failures into downstream components (metrics ingestion, billing pipeline). Goal: implement a tiered load-shedding framework that combines admission-control at the edge, priority queues by customer tier and route, and graceful degradation modes (e.g., fast-fail, reduce-token-generation, cached-prefix fallback) to preserve critical traffic and maintain SLOs. This ticket scopes the design, a minimal implementation for hosted-api and Dedicated proxy, and a phased rollout with safe defaults and metrics-driven thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Backend can drop or deprioritize non-critical requests when regional CPU/GPU queue depth > configured threshold
Priority queue rules support at least three tiers (critical, standard, background) and allow per-customer overrides via account metadata
Admission controller exposes runtime knobs: global threshold, per-queue weights, fast-fail ratio, and slow-path degradation (max tokens or reduced sampling)
Circuit-breaker integration: unhealthy worker pools flip to short-circuit mode and trigger traffic routing to alternate region or model variant
Automated observability: dashboards showing shed rate, request latency by tier, error-budget burn, and runbook links; alerts for >5% shed rate sustained for 5m
End-to-end tests simulate overload and verify critical-tier success rate >= 99% while non-critical tier can be shed
Rollout must support gradual percentage ramp with escalation and rollback hooks (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
design_decision_summary: We will implement an admission-control layer that consults a lightweight priority-index on each request (derived from API key metadata + route). Admission control operates before request enters KV cache or batching buffer to minimize wasted compute. Three degradation modes will be supported: 1) fast-fail (HTTP 429 with retry-after); 2) degraded generation (strict token cap + lower temperature + shorter max_output); 3) cached-prefix fallback (if prefix cached, return from cache or rerank cached completions). Circuit breakers sit on top of worker pool health metrics (queue depth, recent error-rate) and will mark pools as 'short-circuit' after exponential backoff. Traffic routing will prefer local region, but when short-circuited will route to warm regional failover or a cheaper quantized model variant as configured per customer. Knobs exposed via runtime config and Console feature flags for safe rollout.
implementation_plan: Week 1: proto admission-control middleware in hosted proxy; add priority header extraction and basic fast-fail logic (Marco)
Week 2: implement per-queue counters, weight-based dequeuing, and attach shed metrics (Aisha + SRE)
Week 3: integrate degraded generation mode in runtime (max_tokens clamp + sampling override) and add control plane flags
Week 4: circuit-breaker logic by pool with backoff and regional routing fallback; add unit/integration tests
Week 5: end-to-end chaos tests and SLO verification in staging; create dashboards and alerts (Observability)
Week 6: canary rollout on 5% traffic, monitor, then 25%/50% if stable; postmortem and tweak thresholds
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: runtime.feature.load_shedding = false by default
Canary 1 (5%): enable for non-critical customers only, monitor shed-rate and p95 latency for 30m
Canary 2 (25%): enable for standard tier, keep critical-tier protected and require manual approval
Full ramp (50->100%): flip for Dedicated tenants with opt-in; add per-tenant overrides in Console
Rollback: immediate disable of runtime flag or per-region traffic shift to fallback region; runbook steps documented
Post-rollout: tighten alerts for unexpected customer impact and schedule follow-up to tune thresholds
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: shed_count_total{tier}, shed_rate{tier}, admission_queue_depth{region,pool}, circuit_breaker_state{pool}
Dashboards: Load Shedding Overview (global), Tiered SLA heatmap, Per-region failover map
Alerts: P0 if critical-tier success rate < 99% for 5m; P1 if shed_rate_total > 5% sustained for 10m
SLO linkage: link shed_rate to error budget burn policy; automatically pause aggressive shedding if SLA for a paying customer is at risk
Runbook: flowchart to disable shedding for a specific customer, re-route traffic, or increase capacity
